costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz OM656 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM656 engine typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the AdBlue dosing module, the EGR cooler, and the 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG). Because the OM656 is a highly complex modern common-rail unit, recon specialists will typically verify the ISG health, update all software maps, and replace the EGR cooler as standard. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM656 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue System Faults
items.whatHappens: The AdBlue dosing module, heater, or NOx sensors can fail, leading to warning lights, restricted performance (limp mode), and eventually a no-start condition if the tank is depleted and the system is locked out by the ECU.
items.repairVsReplace: Often resolved by replacing the dosing module or NOx sensor, which is a standard repair. If the tank heater or pump has failed, a full tank assembly replacement may be required.

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks
items.whatHappens: The internal matrix of the EGR cooler can crack, allowing coolant to mix with exhaust gases or enter the intake manifold. This leads to unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential hydrolock if severe.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement is a standard repair. If caught early, it prevents catastrophic internal engine damage.

items.title: Mild-Hybrid (ISG) Integration Issues
items.whatHappens: The Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) is a complex 48V component. While generally reliable, software glitches or electrical faults can cause start-stop malfunctions, reduced EQ Boost assistance, or warning lights.
items.repairVsReplace: Most ISG issues are resolved via software updates or replacing the 48V auxiliary battery. Full ISG replacement is rare but costly if the unit itself fails.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM656 is generally considered a highly robust and reliable modern diesel, representing a significant refinement and durability step up from the older V6 OM642 it replaced. Units maintained with strict AdBlue top-ups and regular oil changes routinely exceed 150,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM656
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM656 is sometimes confused with the older 3.0L V6 OM642 or the smaller 2.0L inline-4 OM654. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM656 features a specific modular inline-6 design, distinct 48V mild-hybrid wiring looms, and specific ECU mapping that will not function correctly if swapped with an OM642 or OM654 without extensive and costly modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM656 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM656 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof that the AdBlue system, EGR cooler, and 48V ISG are in good working order. Given the complexity of modern hybrid emissions systems, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM656 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by verifying the AdBlue dosing module, replacing the EGR cooler, and refreshing all critical seals, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM656 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage W223 S-Class or W167 GLE hosts where maximum longevity and originality are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM656 engine is installed by specialists familiar with modern Mercedes CDI and mild-hybrid systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM656 is typically found in modern W213, W222/W223, and W167 vehicles valued between £15,000 and £60,000+, a full replacement is highly financially viable and comfortably within the host vehicle's value . Replacement cost rarely exceeds the scrap threshold for these modern chassis, making a reconditioned unit a highly sensible investment.

items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes OM656 engine typically costs between £3,200 and £5,500 for supply only . items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM656 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are AdBlue system faults, EGR cooler leaks, and occasional mild-hybrid (ISG) integration issues. AdBlue dosing module or NOx sensor failures trigger limp mode, while EGR cooler cracks can lead to unexplained coolant loss and white smoke from the exhaust. → Get quotes for a rebuilt OM656 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the OM656 engine?

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM656 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned OM656 is strongly recommended over a used unit.
